name: Dr. Meera Joshi
profile_summary: Dr. Meera Joshi is an Associate Professor in the Department of Artificial Intelligence and a core investigator at the Bio-Computing and Medical Informatics Centre. Her research centers on deep learning architectures applied to clinical decision support systems, high-density genomic analysis, and medical image reconstruction. Dr. Joshi's research addresses the critical challenge of high-noise and incomplete data in clinical settings. Her team develops generative adversarial frameworks to super-resolve low-dosage CT scans and construct predictive diagnostics for cardiac anomaly detection. She has established strong cooperative ties with premier oncology centers, co-developing models that predict treatment resistance in patient cohorts. Dr. Joshi serves as an associate editor for several bio-engineering journals and has received awards for her work on deep learning for personalized medicine. She is committed to translating AI theories into clinically validated diagnostic assistance software.

current_projects.title: OncoPredict: Deep Learning for Dynamic Cancer Progression Modeling
current_projects.description: Utilizing recurrent and graph neural systems to model patient tumor progression and predict therapy resistance over time.

current_projects.title: LowDoseResolve: Super-Resolution Synthesis for Low-Dosage Clinical Scans
current_projects.description: Designing customized generative diffusion architectures to synthesize high-resolution diagnostic slices from noisy CT scans.

publications.title: Super-Resolving Low-Dosage CT Scans using Generative Diffusion Models
publications.abstract: We formulate a clinical diffusion framework capable of reconstructing high-frequency structural features from low-dosage CT inputs. Radiologist evaluations confirm a 92% diagnostic parity with standard high-exposure scans.

publications.title: Predicting Therapy Resistance in Oncological Cohorts via Graph Networks
publications.abstract: We construct graph neural networks (GNNs) to model the spatial relationship of tumor cells. Our framework integrates genomic sequences and pathology scans to predict drug resistance with high statistical confidence.

publications.title: Deep Recurrent Classifiers for Real-time Electrocardiogram Anomaly Auditing
publications.conference_or_journal: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
publications.abstract: We propose a lightweight recurrent model with spatial attention designed to run on clinical monitors. Our model processes high-density ECG signals, identifying ventricular arrhythmias with high sensitivity.
